name: Longest busy stretch
brief:
A call centre logs each call by its start and end second, and a call is live from its start up to but not including its end. The line is busy while at least `k` calls are live. Find the length in seconds of the longest unbroken busy stretch, or 0 if the line is never that busy.

The whole input arrives as one string `text`:

- line 1: `n k`, the number of calls and the busy threshold;
- then `n` lines, each `start end`.

Return the length as a string. Lines may carry extra spaces, and the text may end with blank lines.

Write `solve_peak_calls(text)`.

Example. For `"3 2\n0 10\n5 15\n10 20\n"` and `k = 2`, two calls are live from 5, and at 10 the first ends as the third starts, so two stay live until 15. The longest busy stretch runs from 5 to 15, so the answer is `10`.
constraints: $O(n \log n)$ time is the target. Counting the live calls afresh at every second is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Turn each call into two events, `+1` at its start and `-1` at its end, and sort them. Apply every event at one second together, then check whether the live count is at least `k`.

examples.note: Two calls are live from 5 to 15, and the hand-over at 10 does not break the stretch.
One call is live at every second from 0 to 9, so the hand-over at 5 does not break the stretch.
The two calls never overlap, so two are never live and the answer is 0.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Sorting the starts and ends as events means the live count changes only at an event, so one pass finds every stretch with at least `k` calls live.
Apply every event at one second before testing the count. Testing after each single event splits a stretch at a hand-over, where one call ends as another starts.
Sorting the $2n$ events costs $O(n \log n)$, with $O(n)$ space.

planted.slip: It handles each event one at a time, so a call ending as another starts at the same second briefly drops the count and splits one busy stretch in two.
